method.summary: How long does one keyless documentation call to this server take, from a caller that is nobody in particular? Fifteen calls to `search_mintlify`: five plain-language questions inside the scope the server's own tool description claims, each sent three times, in three rounds round-robin across eight of the nine solutions measured, so a slow minute on this container's network falls across all of them rather than on one. Median 823.5 ms, min 687.4, max 5447.8, IQR 687.4; round medians 1109.5, 716.3, 1722.8 ms; 0 failures. WHAT THIS IS NOT: a server-side latency. Every number includes this container, its HTTP proxy and one day's public internet from a single vantage point; three rounds notice an outlier and cannot characterise a distribution over time. Response size is not controlled and is published beside every duration (median 14826 bytes of text here): a server returning more text is doing more work on the wire, which is a property of the corpus, not of its speed. NO BASELINE, deliberately: the job says 'within the agent's turn', which is not a number, and inventing one so the coverage table resolved to supports or contradicts would be filling a cell to make the map look finished. This record is a measurement; the adjudication is the reader's. NO RANKING and no comparison with the other records filed from this run: the question sets differ because the corpora differ. The protocol was pre-registered before any call was sent.
method.dataset: Five questions, each sent three times: How do I configure navigation in docs.json?; How do I add a custom domain to a docs site?; How do I generate API reference pages from an OpenAPI spec?; How do I preview docs locally with the CLI?; How do I add authentication to a docs site?

results.metric: median round-trip of one documentation call
results.interval: n=15, IQR 687.4 ms, one container, one day
